key_insight: No single generative model or sampling strategy consistently produces the most diverse set of valid answers across prompts; training a lightweight router to choose which model or sampling policy to use per input yields substantially better coverage of unique high-quality responses.
problem_solved: How to comprehensively elicit a diverse, high-quality set of valid answers for prompts that admit many correct responses, when relying on a single model or uniform sampling wastes budget and misses unique answers.
method: Define a metric called diversity coverage: total quality of each unique answer in a predicted set relative to an oracle set of the same size.
Train a learned router that, given an input, selects which base model and/or sampling policy should generate samples for that prompt to maximize diversity coverage under a fixed sampling budget.
Optimize allocation using validation feedback (reward signals or quality estimates) to route inputs to the model/policy mix that produces complementary, non-redundant answers.
impact: Practitioners can get broader, higher-quality coverage of valid outputs without increasing total sampling cost by routing prompts to specialized models/policies—useful for creative generation, pluralistic QA, data curation, and systems that must satisfy diverse user intents.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: prompt → learned router → multiple models/policies → aggregated unique answers
Line/bar chart: diversity coverage vs. number of samples comparing single-model, ensemble (uniform), and routed allocation
Example panel: same prompt with sets of answers from single model (redundant) vs routed approach (diverse, high-quality uniques)
Training flowchart: computing diversity coverage on validation, updating router, and re-allocating sampling budget
paper_title: No Single Best Model for Diversity: Learning a Router for Sample Diversity
paper_authors: Yuhan Liu, Fangyuan Xu, Vishakh Padmakumar, Daphne Ippolito, Eunsol Choi
